lesson_scope: Equating a line y = mx + c to a parabola y = ax^2 + bx + d, forming the quadratic intersection equation, setting discriminant D = 0 for tangency (1 point of contact), finding unknown constant (gradient m or y-intercept c), and determining the single point of contact (x, y).

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: finding horizontal line constant c for tangency D = 0.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of equating y = c and setting D = 0.

hints: Equate the horizontal line $y = c$ to the curve: $x^2 - 6x + 13 = c$.
Set the discriminant to zero for tangency: $(-6)^2 - 4(1)(13 - c) = 0 \implies 36 - 52 + 4c = 0 \implies 4c = 16 \implies c = 4$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the curve and the line to set up the intersection equation:
$$x^2 - 6x + 13 = c$$
$$x^2 - 6x + (13 - c) = 0$$

Solve for the constant $c$:
$$4c - 16 = 0 \implies 4c = 16 \implies c = 4$$

ai_rubric.observable: Equates curve to line and sets $D = (-6)^2 - 4(1)(13 - c) = 0$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: finding y-intercept c for slanted line tangency.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of solving for y-intercept c.

hints: Equate the line $y = 2x + c$ and parabola $y = x^2 + 1$: $x^2 + 1 = 2x + c$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the line and parabola and collect all terms on one side:
$$x^2 + 1 = 2x + c$$
$$x^2 - 2x + (1 - c) = 0$$

Set the discriminant to zero for tangency:
$$D = (-2)^2 - 4(1)(1 - c) = 0$$
$$4 - 4 + 4c = 0$$

Solve for $c$:
$$4c = 0 \implies c = 0$$

ai_rubric.observable: Equates to get $x^2 - 2x + (1 - c) = 0$ and sets $(-2)^2 - 4(1)(1 - c) = 0$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: finding gradient m of line passing through origin.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of finding gradient m for tangency.

hints: Set the discriminant to zero: $(-m)^2 - 4(1)(9) = 0 \implies m^2 - 36 = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the line $y = mx$ and curve $y = x^2 + 9$:
$$x^2 - mx + 9 = 0$$

Set the discriminant equal to zero:
$$D = (-m)^2 - 4(1)(9) = 0$$
$$m^2 - 36 = 0$$

Solve for both possible gradients:
$$m^2 = 36 \implies m = 6 \quad \text{or} \quad m = -6$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: calculating the coordinates of the point of contact from repeated root.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of determining coordinates of tangency point.

hints: Solve the perfect square $(x - 3)^2 = 0$ to get $x = 3$.
Substitute $x = 3$ into either equation: $y = 3^2 = 9$. Point of contact is $(3, 9)$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the line and curve to find the intersection $x$-coordinate:
$$x^2 = 6x - 9$$
$$x^2 - 6x + 9 = 0$$
$$(x - 3)^2 = 0 \implies x = 3$$

Find the corresponding $y$-coordinate:
$$y = 3^2 = 9 \quad \left(\text{or } y = 6(3) - 9 = 9\right)$$

State the coordinates of the point of contact:
$$(3, 9)$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: tangency to an inverted parabola.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of equating with negative leading coefficient.

hints: Rearrange to a positive $x^2$ coefficient: $x^2 - 6x + (5 + k) = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the line and curve, and rearrange to standard quadratic form:
$$-x^2 + 4x - 5 = -2x + k$$
$$x^2 - 6x + (5 + k) = 0$$

Apply the tangency condition $D = 0$:
$$D = (-6)^2 - 4(1)(5 + k) = 0$$
$$36 - 20 - 4k = 0$$

Solve for $k$:
$$16 - 4k = 0 \implies 4k = 16 \implies k = 4$$

ai_rubric.observable: Equates to get $x^2 - 6x + (5 + k) = 0$ and sets $(-6)^2 - 4(1)(5 + k) = 0$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: tangency with non-monic leading coefficient a = 2.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of tangency condition on non-monic parabola.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the line and parabola and rearrange to standard form:
$$2x^2 + c = 4x - 1$$
$$2x^2 - 4x + (c + 1) = 0$$

Apply the tangency condition $b^2 - 4ac = 0$:
$$D = (-4)^2 - 4(2)(c + 1) = 0$$
$$16 - 8(c + 1) = 0$$

Solve for the constant $c$:
$$8(c + 1) = 16 \implies c + 1 = 2 \implies c = 1$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: line tangent to a quadratic, requiring discriminant setup to solve for constant c.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires equating line and curve and solving D = 0 for intercept c.

hints: Equate line $y = 4x + c$ and curve $y = x^2 + 8$: $x^2 + 8 = 4x + c$.
Set the discriminant to zero: $b^2 - 4ac = (-4)^2 - 4(1)(8 - c) = 0 \implies 16 - 32 + 4c = 0 \implies c = 4$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the line and curve equations to form the quadratic intersection equation:
$$x^2 + 8 = 4x + c$$
$$x^2 - 4x + (8 - c) = 0$$

For the line to be a tangent, the discriminant must be zero ($D = 0$):
$$D = (-4)^2 - 4(1)(8 - c) = 0$$
$$16 - 32 + 4c = 0$$

Solve for the constant $c$:
$$4c = 16 \implies c = 4$$

ai_rubric.observable: Equates line and curve to obtain $x^2 - 4x + (8 - c) = 0$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: finding two possible values of gradient m for line tangent to a parabola.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires setting discriminant of intersection equation to zero to find gradient m.

hints: Set the discriminant equal to zero for tangency: $(-m)^2 - 4(1)(4) = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the line and curve equations and set to zero:
$$x^2 + 3 = mx - 1$$
$$x^2 - mx + 4 = 0$$

Apply the condition for tangency ($b^2 - 4ac = 0$):
$$(-m)^2 - 4(1)(4) = 0$$
$$m^2 - 16 = 0$$

Solve for both possible values of the gradient $m$:
$$m^2 = 16 \implies m = 4 \quad \text{or} \quad m = -4$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: finding intercept constant for inverted parabola tangency and determining point of contact coordinates.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires finding parameter k for tangency to an inverted parabola.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the line and curve equations and rearrange to standard form:
$$-x^2 + 6x - 1 = 2x + k$$
$$x^2 - 4x + (k + 1) = 0$$

Apply the tangency condition $D = 0$:
$$D = (-4)^2 - 4(1)(k + 1) = 0$$
$$16 - 4k - 4 = 0 \implies 4k = 12 \implies k = 3$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires finding coordinates of point of contact.

hints: Solve $(x - 2)^2 = 0$ to get the repeated root $x = 2$.
Substitute $x = 2$ into the line equation: $y = 2(2) + 3 = 7$. Contact point is $(2, 7)$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $k = 3$ into the intersection quadratic equation:
$$x^2 - 4x + 4 = 0$$
$$(x - 2)^2 = 0 \implies x = 2$$

Find the corresponding $y$-coordinate using the line equation:
$$y = 2(2) + 3 = 7$$
$$\text{Point of contact: } (2, 7)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes $k = 3$ into $x^2 - 4x + 4 = 0$ to find repeated root $x = 2$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: x-axis tangency (y = 0) determining parameter k and sketching the resulting curve.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires finding positive parameter k for which x-axis is tangent to curve.

hints: The $x$-axis has equation $y = 0$, so tangency means $2x^2 + kx + 8 = 0$ has a repeated root.
Set the discriminant to zero: $k^2 - 4(2)(8) = 0 \implies k^2 - 64 = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
The $x$-axis is the line $y = 0$. Tangency requires the discriminant of $2x^2 + kx + 8 = 0$ to equal zero:
$$D = k^2 - 4(2)(8) = 0$$
$$k^2 - 64 = 0$$

Solve for the positive constant $k$:
$$k = \sqrt{64} = 8$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires identifying contact point and sketch.

hints: The contact point on the $x$-axis is $(-2, 0)$.
Sketch an upward-opening parabola with vertex touching the $x$-axis at $(-2, 0)$ and $y$-intercept at $(0, 8)$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $k = 8$ into the equation and factorise:
$$2x^2 + 8x + 8 = 2(x^2 + 4x + 4) = 2(x + 2)^2 = 0$$
$$\text{Contact point on } x\text{-axis is } (-2, 0)$$

State the key features for the sketch:
$$\text{Vertex / contact point: } (-2, 0)$$
$$y\text{-intercept: } (0, 8)$$
$$\text{Shape: U-shaped parabola tangent to the } x\text{-axis at } (-2, 0).$$

ai_rubric.observable: Correct sketch of upward-opening parabola tangent to $x$-axis at $(-2, 0)$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: finding two gradients and two contact points for line tangent to parabola.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires finding two gradients m from quadratic discriminant condition.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the line and curve and collect terms into standard quadratic form:
$$x^2 - 2x + 6 = mx + 5$$
$$x^2 - (2 + m)x + 1 = 0$$

Set the discriminant to zero for tangency:
$$D = (-(2 + m))^2 - 4(1)(1) = 0$$
$$(m + 2)^2 - 4 = 0$$
$$(m + 2)^2 = 4 \implies m + 2 = \pm 2$$
$$m = 0 \quad \text{or} \quad m = -4$$

ai_rubric.observable: Equates to get $x^2 - (2 + m)x + 1 = 0$ and sets $(2 + m)^2 - 4 = 0$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires finding coordinates of both points of contact.

walkthrough.text:
For $m = 0$:
$$x^2 - 2x + 1 = 0 \implies (x - 1)^2 = 0 \implies x = 1$$
$$y = 0(1) + 5 = 5$$
$$\text{Point of contact: } (1, 5)$$

For $m = -4$:
$$x^2 + 2x + 1 = 0 \implies (x + 1)^2 = 0 \implies x = -1$$
$$y = -4(-1) + 5 = 9$$
$$\text{Point of contact: } (-1, 9)$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: line through external fixed point tangent to parabola, solving quadratic discriminant and finding distinct contact points.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires finding tangent slopes from fixed external point.

hints: Set the discriminant to zero: $[-(4 + m)]^2 - 4(1)(9) = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the line and curve equations:
$$x^2 - 4x = mx - 9$$
$$x^2 - (4 + m)x + 9 = 0$$

Set the discriminant to zero for tangency:
$$D = (-(4 + m))^2 - 4(1)(9) = 0$$
$$(m + 4)^2 - 36 = 0$$
$$(m + 4)^2 = 36$$

Solve for both values of $m$:
$$m + 4 = \pm 6$$
$$m = 6 - 4 = 2 \quad \text{or} \quad m = -6 - 4 = -10$$

ai_rubric.observable: Equates curve and line to obtain $x^2 - (4 + m)x + 9 = 0$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: two-parameter tangency proof and proving locus of contact points is a horizontal line.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires algebraic proof linking parameters c and p for tangency.

hints: Divide by $4$: $(p - 1)^2 - (p^2 + 5 - c) = 0 \implies p^2 - 2p + 1 - p^2 - 5 + c = 0 \implies c = 2p + 4$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the line and curve equations:
$$x^2 + 2px + (p^2 + 5) = 2x + c$$
$$x^2 + 2(p - 1)x + (p^2 + 5 - c) = 0$$

Set the discriminant to zero for tangency:
$$D = [2(p - 1)]^2 - 4(1)(p^2 + 5 - c) = 0$$
$$4(p^2 - 2p + 1) - 4(p^2 + 5 - c) = 0$$

Divide by $4$ and simplify:
$$p^2 - 2p + 1 - p^2 - 5 + c = 0$$
$$-2p - 4 + c = 0 \implies c = 2p + 4$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Requires finding locus of contact point.

hints: The intersection equation is $(x + (p - 1))^2 = 0$, giving repeated root $x = -(p - 1) = 1 - p$.
Substitute $x = 1 - p$ and $c = 2p + 4$ into the line equation $y = 2x + c$.
Because the $y$-coordinate is always $6$ regardless of $p$, all points of contact lie on the horizontal line $y = 6$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the $x$-coordinate of the point of contact from the repeated root:
$$(x + (p - 1))^2 = 0 \implies x = 1 - p$$

Conclude that the locus is the line $y = 6$:
$$\text{The contact point has coordinates } (1 - p, 6).$$
$$\text{Since } y = 6 \text{ is constant for all } p, \text{ all points of contact lie on the horizontal line } y = 6.$$

ai_rubric.observable: Concludes that because $y = 6$ independent of $p$, all points of contact lie on the line $y = 6$.
